news.title: Gallery: Baltimore's screamer fires Blues to top of the league!
Sonia Bompastor praises Chelsea character after Man City victory
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor praised her players' character and defensive performance after Chelsea beat Manchester City 1-0 at Stamford Bridge to move to the top of the Women's Super League. Sandy Baltimore's stunning strike on the stroke of half-time proved decisive, as the Blues claimed a huge three points against our title rivals and ended City's unbeaten start to the season. The victory was particularly important after Chelsea dropped points in the league against Everton last weekend and suffered a Champions League stalemate against BK Hacken during the week. Bompastor was delighted with the response from her players, highlighting the hard work and determination required to keep a dangerous City attack at bay. 'I am happy. Credit to my players. We showed a lot of character coming into the game today. It was not easy, especially on the back of the points we dropped in the league last weekend and in the Champions League,' the Chelsea head coach said. 'The players worked really hard, and the performance was a good one. Especially not to concede a goal against this side, Manchester City, so I think it was a strong defensive performance.' One of the standout performers was young defender Veerle Buurman, who came on after just 12 minutes following an injury to Kadeisha Buchanan. She helped keep City's leading scorer Khadija Shaw quiet throughout the contest. Bompastor was particularly pleased with the way the team dealt with the striker, while also praising Buurman's individual contribution. 'You know, when you come into this game, you try to keep her [Shaw] quiet as much as possible. When it is the case at the beginning of the game, that is good, but you have to do it for the whole game and the 90-plus minutes,' she explained. 'I felt Veerle Buurman had an exceptional game. Being young but being able not to let her have a lot of opportunities was a strong performance, but the whole team had a really strong performance in terms of the defensive aspect.' Bompastor was also asked about Katie McCabe's message to the team to 'play like dogs' before the game, and was happy with whatever approach helped her players deliver on the pitch. 'If that makes them good and happy, then I'm happy for them to play like dogs or cats or whatever they want,' she added. 'We have shown this season that we are doing well in not being easy to break down, and today was another opportunity to show that. To do that against the top teams is a nice feeling.'

news.title: Lucy Bronze on Chelsea's consistency against 'top' Manchester City
news.body_en: Lucy Bronze delivered an outstanding defensive performance as Chelsea beat Manchester City 1-0 at Stamford Bridge to move above our title rivals and take the top spot in the Women's Super League. Sandy Baltimore's stunning strike on the stroke of half-time proved decisive, but Bronze and her defensive team-mates also played a crucial role in keeping City's dangerous attack at bay. The England international reflected on the challenge of facing City's prolific attacking duo, how the Blues restricted the visitors' threat and the consistency that has taken us to the top of the table. Bronze relished testing herself against the best players in the game, and was particularly pleased with how Chelsea dealt with the threat posed by Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw, who have been in fine form for City this season. 'I always say I love playing against top players,' Bronze explained. 'They have two specifically in Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw. They are magic for Man City this season, and they can't stop scoring. 'We had to be dogs in this game because we couldn’t give them any chances. We were very focused on that. I think it was Katie McCabe who might have said that! Just be in them and around them, don't let them get any chances, as we know how good they are as players. They just need one chance to score.' Bronze was particularly impressive in her battle with Shaw, using her experience and strength to limit the striker's opportunities and prevent her from getting into dangerous positions inside the penalty area. Lucy continued: 'She's so strong and powerful, that's a big part of her game. You just have to challenge her as best as you can. We restricted her and her movement. She doesn't need much space to turn and shoot, so we restricted her today to just a lot of long balls around the halfway line.' The Chelsea defender also knows Hemp well from their time together with England, with the pair regularly facing each other in training. That familiarity made the contest an enjoyable challenge, although Bronze knew she would need to be fully focused to keep the winger quiet. Lucy continued: 'She's a great player and someone that I play against a lot with England. In training, we're always against each other, at right-back and left-wing, so I love the challenge. I know what a good player she is, how much she challenges me and how much I need to be focused in a game like today. I think I dealt with it pretty well.' The victory lifted Chelsea to the top of the WSL, one point ahead of City, and maintained our unbeaten start to the season in all competitions. Bronze believes that consistency has been a major factor in the team's strong position, even without one prolific goalscorer leading the way. 'We've been consistent all season, but we just haven't been prolific with goals and a main goalscorer,' Lucy added. 'But we've performed well in every game, arguably not against Everton last weekend, but we have been consistent. 'The team has been consistent even when we have changed line-ups, the same in the Champions League as well. We've built a really good group of players who are constantly there and constantly fighting, and we are always ready. Even when making changes in the first half, we just keep going and going.'

news.title: Chizaram Ezenwata on his goalscoring form and hidden talent
news.body_en: At just 18 years old, Chizaram Ezenwata is already making a significant impression at Cobham. The young forward has enjoyed a superb start to the 2026/27 season, finding the net eight times for Harry Hudson’s Cobham Next Gen side and earning a Premier League 2 Player of the Month nomination back in September. Having stepped up to the CNG squad, Ezenwata has quickly adapted to the demands of PL2 football, becoming an increasingly important figure within the squad. His progress is another step in an exciting journey with the Blues, having developed into one of the side's leading attacking threats since joining the club at 15. While his performances on the pitch continue to attract attention, there is more to the young forward than his goalscoring ability. Away from football, Ezenwata recently surprised supporters with a rather different talent, as a video of him playing the piano attracted plenty of attention online. It is an interest he has held since childhood and offers a glimpse into the person behind the footballer. We recently sat down with Ezenwata to discuss his impressive start to the campaign, his development at Cobham, the responsibility of his role within the squad and his ambitions for the remainder of the campaign. 'I can't complain about the start of the season and the eight goals,' Ezenwata explains. 'I’d like it to be higher but that’s just me as a striker. I’ve been playing up with the Under-21s and I feel like I am confident, getting more comfortable and really growing.' One of his standout performances was in the EFL Trophy against Reading in October, when Ezenwata scored a brace in our 2-0 win at the Select Car Leasing Stadium. Aside from his well-taken goals, what was noticeable was the 18-year-old’s strength and ability to hold up play against senior opposition. Ezenwata revealed that this was an area of his game that he has focused on improving further since stepping up to the CNG side. He said: 'I really enjoyed the Reading game; it was a good challenge for me. Obviously, wanting to play first team, having that experience in the EFL Trophy and managing to get two goals, I’m really proud of myself for that. 'I feel like I've adapted to the conditions, obviously with my physical prowess as well. One of my big developing points is my hold-up play; I’ve been working on it more in training, doing the extras. In terms of my finishing, I'm just carrying that on as well.' Despite only turning 18 in September, Ezenwata has become a key figure in our Cobham Next Gen side, taking on the vice-captaincy and leading by example on and off the pitch. He also wore the captain’s armband against Flora Tallinn in the UEFA Youth League first leg, and popped up with a goal in that game. The Blues striker admitted he feels the responsibility but enjoys the role and having his teammates’ trust. He said: 'It means a lot to have this role, so I’m going to keep pushing. From the start of the season to now, you can see the togetherness has grown. We’re all interlinked as one. Playing together more, we just understand each’s abilities and personalities.' Since arriving at Chelsea, Ezenwata has developed rapidly. Last season, he registered 21 goals and nine assists across all competitions, including the opener in our Under-18 Premier League National Final victory against Manchester City at Stamford Bridge to help us seal the title. That followed an impressive 2024/25 campaign in which Ezenwata was a regular starter for the Under-18s and finished as the team’s top scorer. He has since led the line for CNG and recently signed a new contract, keeping him at the club until at least June 2029. Reflecting on the journey with the Blues so far, Ezenwata said: 'Coming to Chelsea when I was fifteen, I was very excited. My family and I were all proud and Chelsea is the world to me now; being full-time, playing week in, week out and enjoying my football. 'Last season’s final against Man City, winning that final, was my proudest moment so far at Chelsea. The emotions at full time were unreal, seeing everyone coming onto the pitch. 'This season, it’s been signing my new deal. It's another step in the right direction and shows my hard work is paying off, so I'm going to keep working hard and strive for more.' Away from football, Ezenwata remains incredibly talented. His skill for playing the piano recently attracted attention online, which surprised the young forward. Ezenwata told us: 'I didn’t expect that many people to be there; you can see at the end of the video when I was looking around. I started playing when I was four years old, teaching myself with YouTube and learning nursery rhymes. I’ve kept doing it ever since - it helps me relax.' The song Ezenwata performed in the video is his favourite to play as it’s the most recent he’s learned and took ‘a while’ to perfect. However, it’s not the most difficult he’s learned, with Drowning Love by Chasing Kou taking top spot. Looking ahead to the remainder of the season, Ezenwata has set himself the target of becoming Premier League 2 top goalscorer and vows to keep working hard to make it happen. He'll have a chance to add to his growing tally at the end of the month when we face Norwich City.

news.title: Chelsea's Player of the Month for October 2026 revealed!
news.body_en: Morgan Rogers' impressive start to life at Stamford Bridge continued in October, with the forward voted Chelsea's Player of the Month by users of the Chelsea Official App. The summer signing featured in all five of our matches during the month, playing 444 of the 450 minutes available across four Premier League fixtures and our Carabao Cup tie. He helped the Blues secure three league victories and enjoyed his most productive month since arriving in West London. Rogers scored three goals during October, two in the Premier League and one in the cup, as he continued to establish himself as a pivotal member of Xabi Alonso's attack. His regular involvement underlined the importance he has quickly gained within the team, with the forward becoming a consistent presence in our starting line-up. His standout moment came against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, when he opened the scoring with a sensational individual effort. Collecting the ball from Romeo Lavia just inside the centre-circle, the 24-year-old embarked on a powerful run through the heart of the visitors' defence and into the penalty area before delicately lifting his finish over the despairing goalkeeper. It was a goal of exceptional quality and one which was recognised by Blues supporters, with Rogers receiving the Chelsea Goal of the Month award for October. It was the second consecutive month he had claimed that prize, having also been voted September's winner for his volley against Arsenal. The England international's attacking contribution was reflected in his numbers, with ten shots across his five appearances, while he also featured twice for his country during the international break. His willingness to drive forward from midfield and take on opposition defenders has added another dimension to our attacking play, while his ability to operate in different areas of the forward line has made him a valuable option for Alonso. Rogers has made an excellent impression since joining the club in the summer and has already reached ten goal involvements in all competitions this season, underlining the impact he has made in the early stages of his Chelsea career. He finished top of the October Player of the Month poll on the Chelsea Official App with 36 per cent of the vote. Romeo Lavia was second with 30 per cent, followed by Mike Penders on 18 per cent, Pedro Neto on nine per cent and Jordan Henderson on seven per cent.

news.title: Match report: Chelsea Women 1-0 Manchester City
news.body_en: Chelsea moved to the top of the Women's Super League with a huge victory over Manchester City at Stamford Bridge, ending the visitors' unbeaten league record and moving one point clear of them at the summit. Sandy Baltimore's stunning strike in first-half stoppage time proved decisive in a hard-fought contest. The Blues had to withstand considerable pressure after the break, but defended resolutely before City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off for bringing down Alyssa Thompson outside her penalty area. We remained a threat on the counter and came close to adding a second, but Baltimore's goal was enough to secure three precious points. The result maintains our unbeaten start to the season in all competitions and gives us a significant advantage in the race for the WSL title. The early stages at Stamford Bridge were played at a high tempo, with chances at both ends in an entertaining start to the contest. Manchester City created the first opportunity when Khadija Shaw broke down the left and cut the ball back for Aoba Fujino, whose effort went wide of Hannah Hampton's goal. We responded immediately, with Melvine Malard holding off the City defence before laying the ball into the path of Alyssa Thompson, but the American international fired high and wide. City continued to threaten, but Katie McCabe produced an excellent interception in the eighth minute to prevent Fujino from having another sight of goal. We came close to taking the lead two minutes later. Malard beat Iman Beney down the left and sent in a cross, which took a slight deflection, forcing Ayaka Yamashita into an excellent save. There was an early change for the Blues in the 12th minute, as Veerle Buurman replaced Kadeisha Buchanan in defence. Lexi Potter was shown the first yellow card of the afternoon three minutes later after catching Sam Coffey, before Ellie Carpenter used her pace to get away from the City defence on the right. The Australian drove towards goal but dragged her shot wide of the far post. Our attacking threat continued to grow. McCabe played a superb pass inside the full-back to release Thompson down the left in the 21st minute, and her cross found its way to Carpenter at the far post after Malard had been unable to make contact. Carpenter struck first time, but Rebecca Knaak cleared the ball from inside the six-yard box with Malard waiting to pounce. Baltimore then sent a dangerous cross into the area, which Malard narrowly failed to reach, as City struggled to deal with our attacking play. We were enjoying more possession and creating the better opportunities, although a breakthrough remained elusive. City had a rare effort in the 26th minute when Sydney Wamser tried her luck from around 25 yards, but her shot sailed wide of Hampton's goal. There was an injury concern for us when Malard went down in the 34th minute and, unable to continue, was replaced by Aggie Beever-Jones. The Blues continued to press City and eventually had the final say before the interval. Our pressure was finally rewarded in the fourth minute of added time, as Baltimore produced a stunning finish to put us ahead. City had been caught trying to play out from the back, and we took full advantage by pressing high and winning possession in their half. Buurman won an aerial challenge near halfway before Carpenter held off the City defence and carried the ball forward down the right. City briefly regained possession, but Hasegawa was unable to escape the pressure from Carpenter and Kaptein, who won the ball back. Potter laid it off to Kaptein, who found Carpenter on the right. The full-back then picked out Baltimore inside the penalty area. The French international had time to turn and set herself before unleashing a thunderous strike into the top corner, giving Yamashita no chance and sending Stamford Bridge into delirium. It was a wonderful goal and a deserved reward for our growing dominance. We had looked the more threatening side as the half progressed, shading possession and creating the better chances, and Baltimore's late strike gave us the advantage our first-half performance merited. It was to be Baltimore’s final impact on the game with the attacker replaced by Maika Hamano at the break. City immediately tried to find a way back into the contest after the break, but their first effort on target did not come until the 57th minute when Fujino collected a pass from Shaw. Her tame shot was straight at Hampton, who made a comfortable save. After soaking up the pressure, we continued to threaten at the other end, with McCabe playing a wonderful pass to release Thompson. The forward embarked on a winding run before sending a cross into the area, which was intercepted by the City defence. Our fifth corner followed on the hour mark. McCabe's delivery was cleared, but Bronze returned the ball into the box and Kaptein reacted quickest to the loose ball. Under pressure from Yamashita and Shaw, however, her header went just over the crossbar. The visitors then missed a golden opportunity to equalise. Shaw beat Bronze to the ball before lifting the ball over Hampton, but Hemp somehow failed to make contact at the far post, despite the goal seemingly at her mercy. Carpenter's pressure helped put the England international off, and we survived a major scare. City substitute Miedema soon made her presence felt, playing in Shaw, who cut inside Carpenter before seeing her effort blocked brilliantly by the excellent Buurman. We had a huge opportunity to double our advantage in the 71st minute. Thompson did well to keep the ball alive down the left before sending a cross towards the far post, where Carpenter was completely unmarked. However, the Australian could not make clean contact and fired off target with the goal gaping. City kept on pressing with Fujino skipping past McCabe, but Bronze stepped across to block her effort, before our captain produced another vital intervention to deny Shaw as she prepared to shoot. A decisive moment came in the 75th minute when City goalkeeper Yamashita was sent off. The Japanese international rushed out of her penalty area to meet a ball over the top, but the electric Thompson got there first and knocked it past the onrushing keeper, who brought down our forward. The referee had little choice but to show a straight red card, leaving City with ten players for the closing stages. And we came within inches of making our numerical advantage count immediately; Beever-Jones struck the crossbar from the resulting free-kick, a wonderful effort from distance that was so close to giving us a more comfortable final 15 minutes of action. Despite being down to ten players, City continued to push forward in search of an equaliser, with Bronze continuing to lead our defensive efforts, making another important intervention to prevent Shaw from getting a shot away in the 83rd minute. We remained dangerous on the counter, with Beever-Jones firing wide after a fine run down the left six minutes from time. City had one final opportunity when Beney was played in by Beth Mead in the first minute of added time, but the defender fired over under pressure from the hard-working Thompson. A frenetic, high-quality encounter ended with the Blues claiming all three points to move above City and take the top spot in the WSL. The victory takes us to the top of the Women's Super League, one point ahead of Manchester City, who had been unbeaten in the league and across all competitions before today's meeting. It also extends our own unbeaten start to the season and delivers a significant result against the reigning champions at Stamford Bridge. We host Paris Saint-Germain at the Cherry Red Records Stadium on Wednesday evening (8pm KO) in matchday five of the UEFA Women's Champions League. You can buy your tickets here! news.title: Confirmed Chelsea Women line up vs Manchester City
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has made four changes to her Chelsea side for this afternoon's top-of-the-table Women's Super League clash against Manchester City at Stamford Bridge. Following Tuesday's goalless draw against Hacken in the Women's Champions League, the Blues return to domestic action looking to leapfrog City and move to the top of the league table. Hannah Hampton returns between the posts in place of Livia Peng, while there are two changes in defence, with Kadeisha Buchanan and Katie McCabe coming into the starting XI in place of Nathalie Bjorn and Veerle Buurman. Sandy Baltimore also returns to the side, replacing Sjoeke Nusken, who is named among the substitutes. Elsewhere, Lexi Potter retains her place in the starting XI alongside Keira Walsh and Wieke Kaptein, while Alyssa Thompson and Melvine Malard both start once again. Chelsea: Hampton, Carpenter, Buchanan, Bronze (c), McCabe, Walsh, Kaptein, Potter, Thompson, Baltimore, Malard. Chelsea substitutes: Peng, Bjorn, Buurman, Las, Cuthbert, Nusken, Hamano, Brown, Beever-Jones.

news.title: 'Chizzy' Ezenwata on his excellent form for the CNG
Buchanan on togetherness and WSL title focus ahead of Man City visit
news.body_en: Kadeisha Buchanan believes Chelsea have the quality and togetherness to reclaim the Women's Super League title this season – and is determined to help the Blues make a statement against current champions Manchester City this afternoon at Stamford Bridge. We welcome City to SW6 in a contest between the WSL's top two. Only two points separate the teams after nine games, and neither has yet tasted defeat this term. Victory for Sonia Bompastor's side would see us leapfrog City and return to the summit, and Buchanan, who has been part of a Chelsea defence that has conceded just five league goals this term, believes the Blues are ready for the challenge ahead. 'It's at Stamford Bridge, so we're confident,' the Canadian international said. 'I think the last time we played them at Stamford Bridge, we started off defensively strong. And this season, with the stingy back line we have, I think we'll be in a better space. 'If we have that strong start and clean up a few things in defence, I think we'll be very confident in that game.' City arrive in west London boasting an impressive record of their own, with 25 points earned from a possible 27 and Bunny Shaw leading the WSL scoring charts with 12 goals. Buchanan is well aware of the threat posed by the Jamaican forward and believes limiting her opportunities will be crucial to Chelsea's chances of success. 'I think we've got to try to stop the service into Bunny any way possible and be strong physically,' she said. 'I do feel like we've had a good start to this season in both competitions. I think we are in a good space and just hope to keep it like that and improve as the season goes on.' Buchanan also believes our strong start to the campaign has been built on the understanding and togetherness within Bompastor's squad. Seven victories and two draws from our opening nine WSL fixtures have kept us near top spot, and we have also made a strong start to our UEFA Women's Champions League campaign. 'I think the more we work together, the more we move as one,' explained Buchanan.  'It's about team compactness, moving together, knowing our team-mates, knowing how Lucy (Bronze) plays, knowing how Nat (Bjorn) plays, knowing how Veerle (Buurman) plays, knowing how everyone plays on the field so then you can best support them as well.' That collective spirit will be tested against a City side who ended our run of six consecutive WSL titles last season. But while today's opponents represent an obstacle in our pursuit of silverware this term, Buchanan insists the Blues' motivation comes from within rather than from a desire for revenge. 'I can't speak for everyone – it's each to their own – but I don't think it's about them,' she said. 'I think it's about Chelsea and, going off that, I think it's ours to take. 'It [the title] was ours and we lost it. They didn't win it; we lost it. So I feel it's the same this season: it's ours to take if we truly want it, and it's about just not letting it slip this year. 'Win against Man City at home and we're on top. I think after that game, hopefully we get the result we need, we'll be in a really good space.'

news.title: Internationals: Caicedo on target as he leads Ecuador to victory
news.body_en: Moises Caicedo scored Ecuador's second goal as they beat Costa Rica 2-0, with the Chelsea midfielder captaining his country in the victory. The 25-year-old was his usual all-action self in midfield, contributing important defensive work while also getting forward to support Ecuador's attack. His performance was capped in the 83rd minute when he stepped up to take a penalty and put the result beyond doubt. Caicedo struck the ball powerfully and low into the bottom-left corner, giving the Costa Rica goalkeeper no chance, registering his fourth international goal in 66 appearances for Ecuador. The Chelsea midfielder was given the opportunity to rest after his contribution, being substituted immediately after finding the net. His leadership has also been evident at club level this season, with Caicedo having worn the captain's armband for the Blues on several occasions. Chelsea youngster Kendry Paez was also included in the Ecuador squad but did not feature against Costa Rica. Ecuador's next fixture comes on 17 November, when they face Bolivia at 11pm UK time. Meanwhile, none of Chelsea's Argentine trio of Emi Martinez, Valentin Barco and Aaron Anselmino featured in Argentina's 2-1 defeat to Uruguay in an exhibition match. At Under-20 level, Jacob Hall featured for the USA as they took on Japan in Atlanta. The Samurai Blue claimed a 2-0 victory, with both goals already scored by the time Hall was introduced from the substitutes' bench in the 71st minute. The 17-year-old Chelsea academy product was unable to help his side find a way back into the contest. Hall will have another opportunity to impress on international duty in the early hours of Sunday morning, when the USA Under-20s take on Colombia.

news.title: Late Stamford Bridge winners: the semi-final vote
news.body_en: It is now time for Chelsea fans to decide which two late winning goals scored at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League should advance to the final! There have been plenty of last-gasp deciders to enjoy over the years, and now we are asking you to pick your favourite. To help shorten our very lengthy longlist, we limited our selections to Premier League winners. And they must have been scored in the 85th minute or later. In the quarter-final vote, goals from William Gallas, Estevao Willian, Frank Lampard and Cole Palmer advanced to take their place in today's semi-finals. Those four goals are split into two ties. Watch them back and then vote for your favourite on the Chelsea Official App, with the winners progressing to Monday's grand final! Vote for your favourite late Stamford Bridge winners! We’ve also added a few lines on each goal for added context if you need help making your mind up! news.title: Iconic Chelsea shirts reimagined for Christmas
news.body_en: Chelsea’s new Christmas jumpers have arrived, just in time for the festive party season, so you can show your passion for the Blues and your holiday spirit at the same time. Retro is the theme for Christmas at Stamford Bridge this year, with two of Chelsea’s most iconic kits reimagined in Christmas jumper form, producing the kind of knitwear that will really stand out from the crowd at the office party or family lunch on Christmas Day itself. Shop the full range of Chelsea Christmas jumpers here For Christmas 2026, we are taking things back to the turn of the millennium with a distinctive and ever-popular away shirt from the Nineties, as well as the home kit that kicked off Chelsea’s 21st Century with silverware. Christmas is a time for family, and that was also on people’s minds when Blues skipper Dennis Wise carried his infant son up the famous old Wembley steps to collect the FA Cup trophy after our 1-0 victory over Aston Villa in the 2000 final. It was a truly historic moment, providing one of Chelsea and the FA Cup’s all-time iconic images, as well as being the last time anyone would lift club football’s oldest trophy under the twin towers of the traditional home of the English game, before Wembley was demolished and rebuilt. The shirt our legendary captain Wise was wearing as he did so – one of the most popular retro jerseys still frequently seen in the stands at the Bridge – has now been turned into a Christmas jumper in time for this year’s festivities. There have been a few alterations to add a festive touch, with Christmas-themed messaging replacing the sponsors, while on the back the space reserved for players’ name and number reads ‘Merry 26’, paying tribute to another legendary Blues skipper John Terry, who was taking his early steps in senior football wearing the No26 shirt during the 1999/00 campaign. Our other new Christmas jumper offering mimics the unmistakable away kit worn by Chelsea for the 1994/95 and 1995/96 seasons, instantly recognisable both for its bold design and the era it is associated with. The orange and grey became iconic of a hugely important period in Chelsea’s history, when manager Glenn Hoddle rebuilt the club in his image, being the shirt worn during the debut seasons of global stars like Ruud Gullit, Dan Petrescu and Mark Hughes. Those were the campaigns that laid the groundwork and provided the spark for the most successful spell in Chelsea's history. Of course, those are just two of many Christmas jumpers available from Chelsea, with traditional options also on offer for those who prefer to keep things more festive. news.title: OTD: Chelsea 3-0 Wimbledon | 14 November 1998
Key talking points from Sonia Bompastor's pre-Man City press conference
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor faced the media at Cobham ahead of our huge Women's Super League clash against Manchester City on Saturday, and here are the main talking points from what the Blues head coach said. Bompastor answered the assembled journalists' questions about the game, in which the top two teams in the WSL prepare to face off for the first time this season - with just a couple of points separating the sides. The head coach reported that Lauren James and Naomi Girma will be unavailable until the conclusion of this block of fixtures next weekend, prior to the forthcoming international break. And here are the rest of the key talking points from our head coach’s pre-match press conference on Friday as she looked ahead to a mouthwatering contest. ‘From what you could see from the beginning of the season, probably both teams will want to win the game, and both teams will attack to win the game. ‘Probably you will see goals tomorrow, hopefully for everyone, and not too much for us in terms of conceding! ‘It’s never easy to play teams who are sitting in the low block and not really allowing you to find spaces. I think this game will be different, for sure, in terms of space on the pitch. We need to be smart to recognise that and exploit it.’ ‘The two last results have been frustrating for us, so it's good to see from the players' reaction, but also the staff reaction, that we are hungry. ‘We have hunger going into the game tomorrow. We need to keep working, and I'm convinced we'll create opportunities, and we need to make sure we are clinical. ‘Many things can happen when you are in those moments, and we keep working on the pitch, providing details to the players, reviewing the games, trying to understand what we can do even better to make sure we are able to score in every game.’ ‘She's been really good. She's a player who is able to defend but also to attack, as you could see this season. ‘She’s able to run through that outside corridor. She has improved a lot in terms of the quality of her crossing, but also when she gets in the box, the decision-making on the ball. ‘She's scored some great goals and she's making an impact for us. Even if sometimes people think she can be predictable in what she's doing, she's still really good at doing what she does.’ ‘If we go focus too much on her, another player from Man City will find a way maybe to create and score a goal. We know that because they have a lot of quality as a team, but also they have a lot of great individuals. ‘We believe in the quality of the players we have on the pitch as well. We believe in what we are doing as a team also to defend, especially in the box. We proved that already when we played against Arsenal, when we played against Lyon in the Champions League. ‘We were able to not concede much during those games, we took some learnings, and we'll try to apply the same for the game tomorrow.’ ‘In that game, the mental aspects were the most important ones. When you are leading at home by two goals and you have 15 minutes left in the game, I think you can't let the game go the way it went. ‘But it happens. We took the learnings, and what we know from that game and the quality City has on their side, from minute one until the end of the game they have the opportunity to be a good team and to score at any time. ‘So obviously we know we will have to be a good team from minute one until the end of the game, and make sure we are really switched on.’ See the Blues in action against Man City at Stamford Bridge! news.title: Sonia Bompastor named WSL Manager of the Month
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has been named Women's Super League Manager of the Month after guiding the Blues to three victories from our three league matches in October. Bompastor's side enjoyed a perfect October in the WSL, netting 12 goals and conceding just three as we maintained our unbeaten start to the campaign. The month began with an impressive 3-0 win away at West Ham United, before the Blues returned to Stamford Bridge following the international break to secure a thrilling 6-2 victory over London rivals Tottenham Hotspur. That derby triumph marked Bompastor's 50th WSL match in charge of Chelsea, with the Blues head coach setting a new WSL record of 125 points from her opening 50 games. In our final league fixture of October, we came from behind to claim a 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace, with Melvine Malard scoring twice in the second half to secure all three points. It is the fifth time Bompastor has received the WSL Manager of the Month award since taking charge in the summer of 2024.

news.title: Bompastor updates on James and Girma availability ahead of Man City
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor confirmed that Lauren James and Naomi Girma are progressing well on their return from injury, but she expects our next match against Manchester City to be too soon for them to be involved. Chelsea face a huge Women’s Super League fixture on Saturday, when we host Manchester City at Stamford Bridge in a top-of-the-table clash. After dropping WSL points for the first time since our opening game of the season, we now sit two points behind leaders Man City, but can retake first place with a home win this weekend. However, the Blues will have to do so without the help of James or Girma, after our manager gave an update on the progress of their recovery from injury. ‘I think LJ is good, but I don’t think we expect to see her in this block,’ said Bompastor, in her pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon. ‘That’s the same for Nay. She’s now more in advance, not far from starting again to train with the team. ‘So both of them are doing good, but we won’t see them in this block with us.’ Even without those two, Bompastor still has plenty of talent at her disposal for this massive WSL fixture, and is confident her team has what it takes to secure what could be a crucial victory in the title race in front of our home support at the Bridge. ‘In terms of that the two teams are unbeaten, it is an important game between two teams that are performing at a really good level, but not the only ones obviously. ‘I think tomorrow it’s a game worth three points, like the other ones, but in terms of the psychological aspects, the team that is able to win will take maybe a psychological advantage. ‘So we are playing at home and we approach every game the same, tomorrow won’t be different. We want to come to the game and bring some confidence, but also try to win the game. I know we have the ability to do that so we will try our best. ‘The game plan is ready. We’ve only had a few training sessions after the Hacken game, but I feel the team is in a good place and ready for the game tomorrow.’ Secure your seat at the Bridge to cheer the team on against Man City! Tickets are still available.

Favourite late winners: The quarter-final results!
news.body_en: We can now reveal which four memorable Chelsea late winning goals have advanced to the semi-finals in our vote held on the Chelsea Official App. We asked supporters to choose their favourite late Premier League winner at Stamford Bridge in four separate pairings. The first to progress was William Gallas, whose spectacular strike against Tottenham edged out his compatriot Frank Leboeuf with 67 per cent of the vote. It was more clear cut in the second quarter-final, where Estevao's winner against Liverpool last season triumphed with an 89 per cent share over the vote, beating Claude Makelele's goal on the day we lifted the Premier League title for the first time. Our third semi-finalist is Frank Lampard, who sparked pandemonium at the Bridge when he completed a late comeback against Stoke in 2009. That received 61 per cent of the vote when paired with Willian's decider in a 1-0 win over Everton six years later. Cole Palmer also advanced, with his late, late deflected strike in the 4-3 epic with Manchester United two-and-a-half years ago. He beat off competition from Fernando Torres, who settled a top-of-the-table clash against Manchester City in 2013. Make sure to return tomorrow (Saturday) to cast your vote in the semi-finals!

news.title: Mike Penders save voted Premier League’s best
news.body_en: Mike Penders has received the Premier League Save of the Month award for October for his stunning stop against Manchester United. The Blues goalkeeper had competition from five others on the shortlist, but the public vote picked Penders’ save as the best in the Premier League during October. The save which claimed the award came late in our 2-0 win over Manchester United at Stamford Bridge, just one week after the 21-year-old’s full league debut. He showed quick reflexes and excellent agility to divert Bryan Mbeumo’s powerful drive onto the crossbar with his fingertips, keeping his clean sheet intact. It wasn’t just the Premier League supporters casting their vote for the award who were so impressed by the Belgian’s reflexes, as he admitted that even some of his team-mates found it almost too good to believe. ‘The ball came so quickly, I didn’t even see it properly,’ said Penders on his award-winning stop. ‘It was just instinct, pure instinct, a reaction. I felt a good touch on my fingertips and, after that moment, I screamed all the positive emotions out. I had to, I was so happy with that moment. ‘Then, after the game, no-one believed me that I touched it! I was like: “Yeah, I touched it, you will see afterwards”. ‘Then it was pretty quickly on Twitter. A team-mate came into the dressing room saying: “He touched it”. I was very happy it was a good angle, because if the angle wasn't right, they could still have some doubts!’ Penders becomes the third Chelsea goalkeeper to receive the Premier League Save of the Month award since it was introduced for the start of the 2022/23 season, following Kepa Arrizabalaga and Robert Sanchez (twice).

news.title: Cuthbert on heavyweight Man City clash and 'pivotal' fans' support
news.body_en: Erin Cuthbert thinks two of the best sides in women's football will make 'punch after punch' when we face off against Manchester City at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. After winning the Women's Super League last season, Man City head coach Andree Jeglertz has guided them to the top of the table once again this season, but the Blues are chasing hard and sit just two points behind after nine games. Saturday's match couldn't be more finely poised, and when we sat down with our captain Erin Cuthbert, she explained exactly why our fans could be the difference-maker in a match where winning and losing will come down to such fine margins. 'The Stamford Bridge crowd have really excelled in the tough moments this season,' said the skipper. 'There have been times when we've been up against it, but that's when the crowd have got us out of that and swung the momentum back in our favour. 'We’re going to need them against Man City because we're not always going to get it our way. The crowd is going to be really pivotal on Saturday. We feed off their energy. We've needed them at times this season, because it hasn't always been plain sailing, despite how many goals we’ve scored and clean sheets we’ve earned. 'Neither side will play for a point; we’ll both be going for the three points, and hopefully that should see the fans turn out in numbers, because they're going to see a game that both sides want to win right until the very end. 'I expect it to be a very high-quality game, but also to be quite edgy at the same time, because both teams want to win, but both teams don't want to lose. So it's a fine balance between whether you go and risk it all, or hold on to what you've got. I know the team will go for it right until the final whistle, and if we're still in it, we'll be going gung-ho, and if we are winning, we'll fight to keep it that way.' Erin Cuthbert is well used to winning silverware at Chelsea. Joining the club in 2016, she only missed out on our first two trophies, and has lifted 18 since then. The Scotland international was a key member of the side that won six consecutive WSL titles before Man City's success last year, and she's determined to see it back in our hands at the end of the campaign. 'It was our trophy for six years before last season, so of course it feels like it's been taken away,' she explains. 'But Man City were rightful winners last year and beat us comfortably in the end. 'There is a degree of wanting to claim what's ours, because it had been ours for so long, but nobody has any given right to the title. It's built through hard work and grinding out wins, good, bad and ugly, across the season, and we're going to need that. 'We know Man City have it just now, so we have to do everything and more. I've been in the position where we've been top of the table, and we've won the league, so I know what it feels like when teams are chasing you. You feel them breathing down your neck. They're coming for you. You feel that in every game. 'It’s a bit different to be the ones chasing. We're part of the chasing pack now, so it's certainly a different mentality, and you're seeing something maybe a bit different this year: that we're so hungry for it.' Those watching will be in for a treat on Saturday, as the Bridge will showcase the very best of what the WSL has to offer as the top two sides battle it out for the three points. If Man City come out to attack, they could break the trend of visiting sides sitting deep in a low block, and that would give our forwards the space to show what they can do. And although for Cuthbert it is just another opportunity to earn three points, another part of her feels that winning the game will make a big statement about our intentions this season. 'Both teams know the quality each other has got at both ends of the pitch,' the captain continues. 'Man City have a very certain style of play. They're not going to sit back and just take pressure from us all game. They're going to come out fighting, and they have really good technical players who can hurt us, but equally we have those players too. It's going to be punch after punch from both sides. 'Their attacking intent could leave spaces that we might not always have in the league, and it opens up a different type of play for a couple of our players in the team to shine. So it's certainly an exciting one, but also one where we're probably going to be a little bit busier defensively, and we expect that. 'It’s something that the team's ready for, because I think defensively we've done really well this season, and I think big credit goes to the backline and everybody else because the job's been monumental so far.' news.title: Once a Blue: Ron Harris
news.body_en: To mark the 82nd birthday of our record appearance maker Ron Harris, we revisit an interview he conducted reflecting on his illustrious Chelsea career. ‘Chopper’ Harris made his Blues debut in 1962 and his final appearance in 1980, 795 games and 14 goals later. He was the captain that lifted our first FA Cup trophy and first piece of European silverware, in the form of the Cup Winners’ Cup. Chopper’s Chelsea journey was quite a ride, so buckle up and enjoy this Q&A… Can you remember your first appearance way back in 1962? I captained the England youth side on the Wednesday and we won some little World Cup, and Tommy Docherty was there with my parents. He told me I'd be in the first team on the Saturday for the game against Sheffield Wednesday. We won 1-0 with Mickey Harrison getting the goal, and I marked a lad called Johnny Fantham. It was a real thrill for me as a 17-year-old lad. You had to bide your time before getting a proper run in the team, didn't you? I did stay in the team for a few games, but we went up to Everton and got hammered. That was it for me until the next year; we got relegated and in the Second Division I got a chance later in the season and we ended up getting promoted. The last game was against Portsmouth and we had to win to go up. I think the final score was 7-0! After that, I think I was a regular until my old team-mate Eddie McCreadie took over as manager. He was very superstitious and I was sub just about every week, occasionally coming on if someone was injured. I think I set a Chelsea record of playing in two games in one day. He thought I could do with a run-out with the reserves, so I went and played for them, and then they got a taxi to pick me up from Stamford Bridge to take me to Millwall. We were 3-0 down and at half-time Jock Finnieston had to come off so I played the second half. I can't imagine too many have done that – and I went to training the next day! Clear something up for us – were you a full-back or a centre-half? Because I wasn't gifted with pace, I enjoyed playing alongside the centre-half. I wasn't a big, dominant fella – I'm 5ft 8in – but you learned how to cope in other ways, using your body in the right way to compete against bigger players. I don't know the exact statistics but I think I played just as many games as a full-back as I did as a central defender. When I first came into the side I just man-marked people: Besty, Greavsie, Denis Law. Wherever they went, I used to follow. If I never touched the ball in a game and they didn't either, I knew I'd done a good job. I have to say, the hardest to man-mark was George Best – well, he was the hardest to try and kick! For a fella who was frail and skinny, he wasn't a coward. He could hold his own against anybody. Right foot, left foot; inside or out, he could take you wherever he wanted. I played against Pele a couple of times, too, but I think Best was the best I ever came across. I don't know, but we all got on very well. There was always a players' lounge and it was only for the players and their wives and girlfriends. There was no animosity if you'd given someone a hard time on the pitch – once the final whistle was blown, everything was forgotten. What I can say is that I'd love to have played with Besty, he gave me a few chasings. Having spent the best part of two decades in the first team, I imagine it must be pretty hard for you to highlight your favourite games for the club... Bearing in mind I didn't score too many during my career, we took on the Hammers just before the 1966 World Cup at Stamford Bridge and I scored two fantastic goals. I sliced one past Peter Bonetti for an own goal and then I went up the other end and hit a fantastic volley past Jim Standen! So that's one game. Then, in the 1971 Cup Winners' Cup run, me and Ossie didn't play in the first leg against Club Brugge when we lost 2-0, but we came back for the return and won 4-0. They were a useful side so that was a memorable game. Obviously the replay against Leeds United in the 1970 FA Cup final is another that stands out more than most, when we beat a tremendous side and became the first Chelsea team to lift the FA Cup. Then there's the European Cup Winners' Cup in Athens – another replay! We lost a goal in the last few seconds of the final, which was played on the Wednesday, and then on the Friday we had a replay and won 2-1. You've picked quite a few cup games there. I guess it sums up Chelsea during your time there, doesn't it? I've always said we were so inconsistent in the league – we could beat anybody on our day, but often when it came to taking on the lesser sides we'd go and get beaten. But with the cup games, the bigger the crowd, the better our star men responded. We had a great team. Peter Bonetti was fantastic in goal and the back four didn't take any prisoners; John Hollins did a great job in midfield while Charlie Cooke and Huddy pulled the strings, and Peter Houseman was a workaholic on the wing; and then you've got Hutch, who was a perfect foil for Ossie. I have to say, Os was the one of the best players I ever played alongside. He was tough as well as incredibly skilful. We had such a camaraderie. If one of the lads was getting a bit of a rough time on the pitch then there'd be one of their mates to help them out. I was privileged to captain a bunch of great lads and tremendous players. The closest you came to winning the league was in the 1964/65 season, when the Blues were top with three games left to play. Was that the year of the Blackpool incident? I've spoken to Tom [Docherty] on many occasions and I think he'll tell you that's the one thing he regretted. We had games against Burnley and Blackpool coming up so we went up there to stay for a few days. Tom said, “You've got to be in at a certain time” and everyone came back, but then some of them snuck out through the fire escape. He ended up sending them home, bringing in a load of youngsters, and we got beaten 6-2 against Burnley. I scored in that game, but I'd have preferred the win. Anyway, that put paid to our chances. The atmosphere between the lads and Tom was off – the whole situation got blown out of proportion and upset the apple cart. If he'd have just fined them a week's wages then I think we'd have probably gone on to win the league. Is that a regret from your time at Chelsea? Not a regret, but it would have been nice. It was the closest we ever came to the title. The balance of the side was the bigger the game, the better they performed. I'm not being disrespectful to some of the less fashionable sides in the First Division, but we just didn't perform against them on the smaller stage. You mention how long you spent at the club, but did you ever consider leaving before finally moving on for Brentford in 1980? I remember captaining England Under-23s when Bill Nicholson was manager and he asked me if I'd be interested in going to the Spurs because they'd love to have me there. But I had absolutely no intention of going there, and they ended up buying Dave Mackay – that was the end of it. Then, when Danny Blanchflower took over as manager we got beaten badly up at Middlesbrough in his first game and things hadn't been going great before that. Danny said to me, “Look, I'll put you in the picture: I'm going with the younger lads. Would you be interested in going to Luton?” David Pleat was the manager at the time and he was someone I'd played alongside at England youth level. Pleaty came round to my house in Epsom for a chat. He told me that I only had to come in to training on a Monday and a Friday – he just needed a bit of an old head for all the youngsters in his squad, someone to look after them. I had two young kids myself at that time and didn't really want to be travelling up there twice a week so I turned them down. Your older brother Allan also played for Chelsea. Does he ever get fed up with being known as Chopper's brother?! I don't think so. In fact, I reckon most people probably remember him for his managerial partnership with Terry Venables at Spurs and Barcelona. He played over 100 games for Chelsea and had the one thing I never did – pace. Was he one of the reasons you joined Chelsea? Yeah. In my day you'd go around all of the clubs so I tried out West Ham, Arsenal, Spurs and others. Then Allan decided on Chelsea and I followed him. When he went there I was a ballboy until I left school. Then I signed for the club. The rest is history – 795 games, 13 or 14 goals depending on you speak to. I'll take the 14, don't worry about that! You almost became a cricketer for Middlesex. What happened? Maybe I'd have done both if the seasons didn't overlap. Ron Tindall always used to miss the start of the football because of the cricket. So I went to see Ted Drake at Chelsea and he offered me £7 per week and a rail pass for the year. I went up to Lord's and was offered £4 per week to join the groundstaff but I had to pay my expenses. I was from a working-class family, so that swayed me. What does it mean to be our record appearance maker? I served under seven managers and what each of them got from me was 110 per cent effort in training and on the Saturday. I'm so proud of playing more games than any other player in the history of Chelsea Football Club and it's a record I don't think will ever be beaten. news.title: OTD: Fulham 1-4 Chelsea | 13 November 2004
Internationals: Rogers on target, Gusto features for France
news.body_en: Morgan Rogers maintained his impressive form by scoring in England's Nations League victory over Croatia this evening, while Malo Gusto started for France against Italy. Rogers has enjoyed an impressive start at Stamford Bridge since following his summer signing from Aston Villa. He has already contributed to ten goals in blue and earned a call-up from Thomas Tuchel for the latest round of England fixtures. The first came tonight at Wembley and Rogers, deployed on the right of the Three Lions' attack, broke the deadlock in the 24th minute. The goal was a poacher's effort, as the 24-year-old produced an intelligent close-range finish after a knock-down from Jude Bellingham. ICE COLD ❄️Morgan Rogers puts the Three Lions in front in the 24th minute 🙌#England #ThreeLions pic.twitter.com/lMCf51fP7F In the second half, Croatia equalised just before the hour-mark through Petar Sucic after the hosts failed to deal with a corner. However, England quickly restored their lead, with Harry Kane converting from the penalty spot on the night he became the Three Lions' most-capped player. Rogers went on to complete the full 90 minutes as England claimed a victory that leaves them second in Group C, three points behind Spain, who they take on this weekend at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid. Meanwhile, in Group A, Malo Gusto started for France in their 3-1 defeat to Italy, for whom Marco Palestra was an unused substitute. Michael Olise opened the scoring for the visitors in the tenth minute, but that advantage was wiped out midway through the first half when Pio Esposito found the net. In the second period, Italy went ahead when Davide Frattesi struck, and Esposito extended an advantage the hosts did not relinquish. Gusto played 77 minutes of the game before being replaced by Sael Kumbedi. The other Group A fixture saw Belgium clinch a 2-1 away win over Turkiye. Blues midfielder Romeo Lavia missed the game due to suspension, while goalkeeper Mike Penders was an unused substitute. At youth level, Shim Mheuka scored twice as England Under-20s claimed a 6-1 win over their  Czech Republic counterparts. Mheuka, currently on loan at Celtic, started alongside fellow Blue Jesse Derry, who is spending the campaign at Sporting CP, and completed his brace before half-time as England established a commanding four-goal lead. The Young Lions added to the second period, during which Chelsea defender Tayo Subuloye was introduced from the substitutes' bench. England remain top of the UEFA Under-20 Elite League, having won their four matches. Portugal are fifth in the table after losing 1-0 to Italy. Blues winger Leo Cardoso was introduced as a late substitute, coming on in the 77th minute, but couldn't help his country rescue a point. And at Under-18 level, Isaac Badu featured in the closing stages as Portugal Under-18s clinched a 1-0 win over Norway Under-18s in friendly action.

news.title: PGA Cup report: Chelsea Women Under-18s 6-0 Ipswich Town
news.body_en: Chelsea Women Under-18s progressed to the quarter-finals of the PGA Cup with a 6-0 victory over Ipswich Town Women Under-21s, with Stevie Sinclair scoring a hat-trick. Sinclair opened the scoring after eight minutes and Sadie Gregory doubled our advantage before the break. The Blues added two goals in as many minutes early in the second half through substitutes Aysia Matabaro and Tess Finn, before Sinclair struck twice more to complete her treble. Leanne Champ’s side controlled possession and combined well to create opportunities throughout Wednesday’s first-round tie. Disciplined work without the ball helped secure another clean sheet. Chelsea went ahead following a move started by Gregory, whose long diagonal pass found Zoe Ciccardini. Keira Johnson’s run beyond the Ipswich full-back created space for Ciccardini to play her into the box. Johnson delivered a first-time pass across goal and the unmarked Sinclair placed her finish into the bottom-left corner. The Blues doubled the lead on 33 minutes following a short free-kick involving Chloe Sarwie and Gabi Storey. Storey’s effort from the edge of the area was parried by the goalkeeper, and Gregory reacted to finish the loose ball. Champ made four changes at half-time, introducing Annie Boichat, Matabaro, Jahmya Putman and Finn for Sophie Leach, Rebekah Pierce, Chelsea N’Drin and Johnson. Matabaro added our third six minutes after the restart. Belle Sullivan and Ciccardini helped work the ball down the left to Putman, who beat her defender and drove inside before finding Matabaro across the edge of the box. She cut inside and finished across goal. The Blues scored again a minute later. Ciccardini intercepted a pass following the restart and found Putman, whose deflected cross reached Storey. Storey picked out Sinclair, who moved the ball wide to Matabaro. Her pass found Finn’s late run into the box, and the substitute finished first time. Sinclair scored her second on 62 minutes after Gregory collected a cleared corner and found Ciccardini on the right. Her deep cross reached Sinclair, who shifted the ball inside her defender and struck low into the bottom-right corner. Emelia Addison replaced Gregory on 70 minutes before Sinclair completed her hat-trick five minutes later. A short corner led to quick combinations between Sinclair, Storey and Sarwie. Receiving Sarwie’s pass, Sinclair drove across the pitch, skipped past two defenders and fired through the crowded penalty area from just outside the box. Chelsea advance to the quarter-finals of the PGA Cup following our first-round victory. The Blues return to PGA Division 1 action on Wednesday 18 November, travelling north to face Manchester United Women Under-21s. Kick-off is scheduled for 2pm. news.title: Home Sweet Home: How the Chelsea Women players are settling in at Stamford Bridge
news.body_en: This weekend's clash with Manchester City will be our sixth Women's Super League game held at Stamford Bridge since we made it our new home. We sat down with four of our Blues to see how they are finding the move... Last season we played four league matches at the Bridge, against Arsenal, Manchester City, London City Lionesses and Manchester United. Now, having already turned out five times in SW6, it feels like an ideal time to check in with our players to see how their new home suits them. The opinions coming from inside the dressing room are unanimous: the move has been a resounding success. Whether it's a settled matchday routine, the atmosphere inside the stadium, or the feeling of butterflies when emerging from the tunnel, it's clear how our players are benefitting from their surroundings. We sat down with three players who remember what it was like to play at Kingsmeadow - Nathalie Bjorn, Kadeisha Buchanan and Erin Cuthbert - and one who has only known the Bridge, summer signing Melvine Malard. Here's what they had to say. 'The locker room is really nice. You're able to really activate and prepare for the game a lot better because there's more space. Obviously, the pitch is really nice and the atmosphere, too. 'The more fans we get, the merrier. A few times they really showed up for us. 'We want to keep that going because we definitely enjoy it when we walk out, and there are a lot of people there. It really boosts us up and gets that really good feeling going that today is going to be a really good game.' 'Stamford Bridge suits our style of play. It’s a bigger pitch, we love the locker room and it’s our home now – it’s our castle. We know it’s a transition process and will take time, but playing at a big stadium is what everyone wants to do. I think the fans really do enjoy it, the same as the players. 'The history of the stadium evokes a lot of feelings. Whether it’s against a top team or a lower team in the league, it still brings that extra fire in you. 'It’s just a feeling you have in your body. It’s a bit hard to explain, but like I said, with all the history and all the good games and the big games we played there before, being able to do that every weekend is a really nice feeling. 'You can hear our supporters throughout the game, which is really nice. They even celebrate if we do a great tackle, so having that support all the time, celebrating the small wins and getting that encouragement from the fans, is really amazing. And when we played Arsenal, for example, there were fireworks and the display in the stands – it was really cool. It creates a great atmosphere when they add those things. 'I would say: “Bring your friends, go to Bottomless at the Bridge, and then watch us play. Have a good time, and some drinks!”' 'It feels good to play at Stamford Bridge. I really love to enjoy playing in front of the fans. I'm a player who likes to celebrate a lot with the fans. In fact, I need to do it! When I score, I need to go over to the fans to make sure everyone has the same pleasure as we do when we play football. 'Everything's more familiar. Last season it maybe sometimes felt like we were playing an away game there, even though we weren't. 'When it’s your home, you've got your familiar settings, you know exactly where you're going, you know where you're eating pre-match, where you're getting treatment, where you're talking to the coaches, where you're doing the tactics. Everything is second nature. 'And on a matchday, the last thing you want as players is to think about anything other than your performance. So having taken all those variables out, I feel like everyone's settled and feels at home at the Bridge now. 'Hopefully the fans feel at home with our performances on the pitch, and their surroundings as well. We want to keep building our fanbase, keep growing, and give them the performances to match that.' Come and cheer on Chelsea Women in Saturday's huge game against Manchester City at the Bridge!

news.title: Malo Gusto joins the ranks of Chelsea’s French centurions
news.body_en: Shortly before heading off to represent his country this week, Malo Gusto made his 100th Premier League appearance for Chelsea, becoming the eighth French international to hit a century for the Blues in that competition. Gusto is currently away as part of Zinedine Zidane’s France squad. They are attempting to hold on to top spot in their UEFA Nations League group and seal qualification for the quarter-finals in their final two games, against Marco Palestra’s Italy tonight and Turkiye on Sunday. In his last game before meeting up with Les Bleus, Gusto came off the bench for Chelsea in our Premier League away fixture at Sunderland, making his 100th appearance for the club in that competition, and 144th in total since arriving from Lyon three years ago. The 23-year-old joins an illustrious list of Frenchmen to have reached a century of games for the club in the Premier League, but who are the other seven Blues to have hit that landmark? Anelka was slow out the blocks for Chelsea, but he more than made up for it in his first full season, in 2008/09. A tally of 19 goals earned him the Premier League Golden Boot award – just the second Frenchman to win it, after Thierry Henry. He netted exactly half of his Premier League goals for the Blues that season, although his intelligent link play was an understated factor during a successful era for the club. The cultured defender was one half of an all-French centre-back pairing with Marcel Desailly that enjoyed plenty of success for club and country. In addition to his defensive strength and quality on the ball, particularly when spraying passes out from the back, Leboeuf also got his share of goals from penalties and some spectacular long-rangers. Famously the holding midfield player who was so good they named his position after him. ‘The Makelele role’ became a common term for a defensive-midfielder in the Premier League, but no one seemed to do it quite as well as him. He was a vital cog in the make-up of two title-winning sides, someone who made the game that much easier for his team-mates. Just like Gusto, the left-winger joined us from Lyon, and did so as the reigning Ligue 1 Player of the Year. Malouda hit top form during our 2009/10 Double-winning season as a key source of both goals and assists. Better was to follow in front of goal the following campaign, as he netted 13 times in the Premier League to finish as our leading scorer. Two-time Champions League winner Desailly joined the Blues shortly before going on to lift the 1998 World Cup with France – alongside Leboeuf – on home soil, and it was not long before Chelsea fans found out just why he was known as The Rock. The defender was at his imposing best in our 2000 FA Cup triumph and during our maiden voyage in the Champions League. He was also the natural successor to Dennis Wise as skipper. Some Chelsea fans have not forgiven Gallas for departing the club for Arsenal as part of the deal which brought Ashley Cole to Stamford Bridge in the summer of 2006, but there is no doubting the key role he played in two title-winning sides. His stunning late winner against Tottenham Hotspur lives long in the memory and he was also part of the defence which set a Premier League low of only 15 goals conceded in 2004/05. Although a quiet character, there was nothing understated about Kante’s performances as we reclaimed our top-flight crown from his former club Leicester City in 2016/17. He was the dominant midfield player in the country and an obvious choice for numerous individual prizes that term. There was also arguably no-one as important as NG in our run to Champions League glory in Porto in 2021, as he was named Man of the Match in virtually every knockout game that season,

news.title: Chelsea Football Club marks 10 years since historic sexual abuse disclosures in football

Their courage brought to light serious failures in the protection of children and young people and prompted significant change across the game. Chelsea Football Club recognises its own place in this history and acknowledges the harm experienced by those who were failed. We recognise that the impact of abuse can be lifelong and that the experiences of survivors must remain at the centre of how this anniversary is acknowledged. As we mark ten years since these disclosures, we recognise everyone affected by abuse, including those who have not felt able to speak about their experiences. We support the FA's survivor-led Voices of Truth initiative and remain committed to listening to those affected, learning from the past and ensuring that safeguarding remains a priority across the Club. We recognise that this anniversary may be difficult for some people. Anyone affected by abuse who wishes to seek advice, share information or access support can contact the following organisations. news.title: Late Stamford Bridge winners: vote for your favourite on the Chelsea Official App!
news.body_en: Nothing beats a late winner at Stamford Bridge. The limbs behind the goal. The players racing to one of the corners to celebrate. The banging of the Matthew Harding Stand billboards. There have plenty to enjoy over the years, and now we are asking you to pick your favourite. To help shorten our very lengthy longlist, we have limited our selections to Premier League winners. And they must have been scored in the 85th minute or later. It was incredibly tough for whittle them down to just eight, so we apologise if your favourite didn’t make the final selection! From Lampard to Leboeuf, Estevao to Willian, there are recent and past classics on momentous days in SW6 that will live long in the memory. We start with the quarter-finals today, with the eight goals split into four ties. Watch them back and then vote for your favourite on the Chelsea Official App, with the winners progressing to Saturday’s semis. The grand final will be on Monday! We’ve also added a few lines on each goal for added context if you need help making your mind up! Frank Leboeuf vs Leicester - 1997 Ruud Gullit's Blues had huffed and puffed all game without reward. That was until the ball rolled invitingly into Frank Leboeuf's path, with the centre-back stepping on to it and larruping a spectacular drive into the top corner. William Gallas vs Tottenham - 2006 On the day the King of Stamford Bridge Peter Osgood died, William Gallas conjured up a dramatic late winner from distance at Ossie's beloved Shed End. Claude Makelele vs Charlton - 2005 Claude Makelele chose a memorable moment to score his first Chelsea goal, getting the party started on the day we lifted the Premier League title for the first time with a rebound from his own spot-kick. Estevao Willian vs Liverpool - 2025 We don't think we need to remind you about Estevao's sliding stoppage-time winner against the reigning champions Liverpool last year! Frank Lampard vs Stoke City - 2009 Trailing 1-0, Juliano Belletti drew us level with two minutes to go before Lampard won it in stoppage time with a rising left-footed drive that had the foundations of the Bridge shaking. The Blues were scrapping hard at the top of the table in 2014/15, so it was looking like two points dropped with a goalless draw against Everton. Step forward Willian, whose low striker from a cleared corner find its way into the bottom corner. Fernando Torres vs Man City - 2013 A top-of-the-table clash was settled by Fernando Torres right at the end after a mistake in the Man City backline gave the striker a free run at goal and a tap-in. Cole Palmer vs Man United - 2024 The second-latest winner in Premier League history - after 100 minutes and 41 seconds - was scored by Cole Palmer at the conclusion of a topsy-turvy epic in which our attacker had already equalised deep into stoppage time.

news.title: UEFA Nations League: What the Chelsea players need
news.body_en: The group stage of the UEFA Nations League concludes over the next week, when seven Chelsea players could be in action for their countries with a chance of featuring in the quarter-finals. Spain and defending champions Portugal became the first teams to book their place in the last eight, during the September and October international break. By the end of this window, the rest of the line-up for March's quarter-finals will be completed, ahead of next summer's final tournament. All seven Blues called up by European teams this week have the chance to be there, going into the final two fixtures of the group stage. Here is what they all need to ensure they have a chance to lift the trophy in June. The first group is packed full of Chelsea interest with Malo Gusto, Marco Palestra, Mike Penders and Romeo Lavia all in contention to feature for their countries, representing more than half of the Blues’ seven players called up for Nations League duty in October. Lavia will be suspended when Belgium attempt to repeat last month’s 3-0 win over pointless Turkiye, but will be available to rejoin Penders and Co for what could be a crucial final fixture at home against Italy. Palestra’s Italy sit second, three points behind leaders France and Gusto, one ahead of Belgium. The French's advantage means that even if they lose that first game – and Italy are the only side to deny Les Bleus victory so far – a point against bottom-placed Turkiye would still guarantee them a quarter-final spot, leaving Belgium and Italy to fight it out for the second qualification place. By then, Hato's international team-mates could have booked their place in the Nations League quarter-finals, going into these games sat at the top of a very tight group. Netherlands vs Greece, Friday 13 November, 7.45pmSerbia vs Germany, Friday 13 November, 7.45pmGermany vs Netherlands, Tuesday 17 November, 7.45pmGreece vs Serbia, Tuesday 17 November, 7.45pm All English eyes will be on veteran captain and this year’s Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane, who is the current Nations League top scorer and will become his country’s all-time appearance maker in his next game. For Chelsea, though, the focus is on fellow attacker Morgan Rogers, Kane’s younger by almost exactly nine years. Spain are already into the quarter-finals and England are on the verge of joining them in second. A point in the Three Lions’ first game against Croatia would seal the deal, avoiding the need to become the first side to take a point off the Spanish. However, with an advantage over third-placed Croatia of six points and a goal difference 21 better, it would take something incredible to deny England a spot in the last eight, regardless. That leaves them with little to play for in their games against Denmark and Wales, although they start a new era under coach Jorge Jesus after long-time captain and national hero Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football. Chelsea duo Pedro Neto and Geovany Quenda will both be looking to stake their claim for a place in that new-look attack after being called up for these concluding fixtures to the Nations League group.
